# mimux — the self-hosted inbox your agents can act on

> A self-hosted email gateway: connect any IMAP mailbox and reach it through
> every interface — a fast, free web client (AGPL-3.0) for humans, and a paid
> automation layer (REST API, MCP server, CLI, signed webhooks; GraphQL on the
> roadmap) for scripts and AI agents. One Go binary, on your own hardware.

Canonical site: <https://mimux.dev/>. This document mirrors the site's content
for language-model consumption. Current release: v0.23.0.

## What it is

mimux is a fast, keyboard-driven email client you run yourself. Point it at the
mailboxes you already have, and read, search, triage and send from one unified
inbox — in the browser or as an installed PWA on your phone. Your mail, your
credentials, your machine.

- Source: <https://github.com/mattmezza/mimux>
- Docs: <https://docs.mimux.dev>
- Account and licences: <https://account.mimux.dev>

## How you get it

One command to boot, zero configuration to run — a container:

```sh
docker run -d --name mimux -p 8083:8083 \
  -v mimux-data:/data ghcr.io/mattmezza/mimux:latest
# then open http://localhost:8083
```

or a checksum-verified binary on your PATH (Linux and macOS, both
architectures):

```sh
curl -fsSL https://mimux.dev/install.sh | bash            # the free client
curl -fsSL https://mimux.dev/install.sh | bash -s -- pro  # + the automation layer
```

1. **Start it.** One container (or one binary), one volume, one port.
2. **Open it.** The first visit walks you through creating your admin account.
3. **Point it at your mail.** Add accounts under Settings → Accounts — OAuth2
   for Gmail and Zoho, app passwords everywhere else. Changes take effect
   without a restart.

Releases carry full three-part semver tags (`v0.23.0`). Images are published as
`:latest`, the exact `:v0.23.0`, and a floating `:v0.23` that tracks patches of
that minor — pin the minor and security fixes arrive, features do not. Pro
images carry the same tags with a `-pro` suffix, plus `:pro`. `mimux upgrade`
replaces a binary install in place (`--check` reports, `--version vX.Y.Z` pins).

One Go binary serves the UI (htmx + Alpine.js + Tailwind) and talks IMAP and
SMTP; one SQLite file holds everything — accounts, credentials, message cache,
sessions, filters, OAuth tokens, API tokens. Back up the directory and you have
backed up everything.

## Features (all free, AGPL-3.0)

- **Unified inbox** across every configured account, plus per-account views,
  conversation threading, unread counts, and the full folder tree per account.
- **Background sync** over IMAP IDLE with polling fallback, one connection per
  account. Gmail and Zoho over OAuth2, everything else over (app) passwords.
- **A folder set, not just the inbox**: every sync cycle walks the inbox, Sent
  and Drafts, plus whatever else you tick per account in Settings → Syncing, so
  mail sent from your phone shows up within the cycle. The inbox syncs last and
  always. Changes made in another mail client are picked up in those folders —
  read/unread and star/unstar on servers that support CONDSTORE, and a message
  deleted or moved away there leaves here too.
- **Search**: instant local full-text search plus on-demand deep IMAP server
  search, streamed back live over SSE as each account answers.
- **Compose**: reply, reply-all, forward over SMTP — plain text, rich text or
  Markdown — with undo-send, scheduled send and optional autosave.
- **Drafts live in the mailbox.** A saved draft is written to SQLite first and
  published to the account's IMAP Drafts folder behind the request, so it is
  waiting in your other clients; a slow or unreachable server costs a retry on
  the next cycle, never the draft. Attachments are part of the draft and go up
  with it. Drafts written in another client are listed here and editable —
  opening one adopts it, so your first save replaces that copy rather than
  leaving a second beside it.
- **Filters & rules**: conditions → actions (move, label, forward, mark read,
  star, delete, notify), run server-side on incoming mail.
- **Keyboard-first**: j/k navigation, e archive, R reply, / search, ? for the
  full shortcut list.
- **PWA & notifications**: installable app with offline fallback; Web Push with
  end-to-end encrypted payloads from your own server, or a POST to an ntfy topic.
- **Calendar invites** render inline; accept or decline in place.
- **AI compose/reply and translate**, optional and bring-your-own-key
  (OpenRouter, Google Translate). Off by default; keys stay in your database.
- **Settings is one page per section** — appearance, reading, composing, quick
  actions, notifications, syncing, search, accounts, signatures, templates, API,
  webhooks, integrations, backup, licence — each at its own URL.
- **Backup = cp**: all state in one SQLite file. Settings → Backup & restore
  also exports a portable JSON copy of the configuration: accounts with their
  credentials and OAuth tokens, preferences, filters, signatures, templates,
  saved searches, trusted senders, labels, API tokens, webhook endpoints and
  per-folder sync choices. No mail travels in it. It holds passwords and API
  keys in plain text — treat the file accordingly.

## mimux pro — the automation layer for agents and scripts

If something other than a human drives mimux, that is the paid layer. All three
interfaces are the same product underneath, authenticated by the same scoped API
tokens from Settings → API:

- **REST API**: accounts, folders, messages (including archive/spam/trash,
  labels and attachment download), search — local or an async deep-search job —
  drafts, send, filters, token introspection and the whole webhooks family, over
  plain HTTP. Self-documented — the binary serves its own OpenAPI spec at
  `/api/v1/openapi.json`, rendered at <https://docs.mimux.dev>.
- **MCP server** at `/api/mcp` (streamable HTTP, stateless; plus a stdio bridge
  via `mimux mcp`): nine tools — `list_accounts`, `list_folders`, `search_mail`,
  `read_message`, `mark_read`, `star_message`, `move_message`, `draft_reply`,
  `send_draft` — plus a `mimux://inbox/summary` resource. The tool list is built
  per request from the token's scopes, so a credential that cannot do something
  is never shown the tool for it.
- **CLI** (`mimux mail`): a thin HTTP client of a running instance — `login`,
  `use`, `logout`, `whoami`, `accounts`, `folders`, `list`, `search`, `read`,
  `mark-read`, `star`, `move`, `draft`, `send`, `webhooks listen`. It mirrors the
  MCP tools one for one, in plain text or `--json`, so the inbox pipes into jq,
  an LLM, or the next script. `mimux mail login <url>` opens a browser to approve
  a token (authorization code with PKCE over a loopback port) — nothing is
  pasted, and the token is an ordinary revocable one from Settings → API.
  `mimux completion bash|zsh` prints a completion script generated from the same
  subcommand registry the binary dispatches on.
- **An agent skill** teaches a coding agent to drive that CLI — auth, the query
  language, scopes, failure modes and the never-send-without-approval rule:
  `npx skills add mattmezza/mimux --skill mimux-cli`.
- **Signed webhooks**: `message.received`, `message.sent`, `message.updated`
  (carrying what changed and whether the origin was `mimux` or `external`),
  `message.deleted`, `sync.error` and `search.completed`, pushed to n8n, Home
  Assistant or your own scripts. Each endpoint has its own secret;
  `X-Mimux-Signature` is `t=<unix>,v1=HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<t>.<body>")` over the
  stored body bytes, so a retry verifies exactly as the first attempt did.
  Failures walk a seven-step ladder over ~24 hours, then the endpoint is
  auto-disabled and you get an email — at most one a day per endpoint. Endpoints
  can be paused and resumed; every one reports delivery stats. The deliveries
  screen and `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` show each attempt with the
  receiver's own answer (first 2KB) and let you replay one with the same
  delivery id. For local development, `mimux mail webhooks listen -forward-to
  http://localhost:3000/hooks` streams live events to your laptop, signed the
  same way, and `-execute ./script.sh` instead runs a program per event with
  the JSON payload on stdin and `MIMUX_EVENT`/`MIMUX_DELIVERY_ID` in the
  environment — nothing is queued while no listener is connected.
- **GraphQL endpoint**: on the roadmap; part of pro when it ships, same price.
- **Guardrails by architecture**: agents draft, but sending is a separate,
  explicit call (two-step send); moving to trash needs an extra confirmation;
  API tokens carry scopes and the tool list an agent sees is filtered by them;
  everything runs on your server, so mail never transits a vendor cloud.

## Pricing

- **The client: €0, forever.** AGPL-3.0. Unlimited accounts and devices.
  Nothing is metered and nothing later moves behind a licence key.
- **Pro annual: {{price:annual:eur}}/year per instance.** Cancel anytime; keeps updating while
  active.
- **Pro perpetual: {{price:perpetual:eur}} once per instance.** Covers every build released within
  one year of purchase; those builds run forever. Builds released after that
  window need a new licence, and nothing forces the upgrade.
- **Trial**: a pro build runs the full automation layer free for 14 days from
  first boot — no key, no card.
- **Licence enforcement is offline**: Ed25519 signature verification inside the
  binary. No activation server, no machine fingerprint, no phone-home. If an
  annual licence lapses there is a 45-day grace period, then only the
  automation layer stops — the mail client never stops working.
- Purchase via Stripe at <https://account.mimux.dev>; 14-day money-back
  guarantee on first purchase.

## Licensing

- Client (`cmd/`, `internal/`, `web/`): AGPL-3.0-only.
- Pro layer (`pro/`): Elastic License 2.0, source-available in the same public
  repository. ELv2 forbids reselling mimux as a hosted service, circumventing
  licence keys, and removing notices.
- `make verify-free` proves the free binary links zero commercial code.
- Full details: <https://github.com/mattmezza/mimux/blob/main/LICENSING.md>.
- `mimux` is a trademark of Matteo Merola.

## Privacy

The application phones home to no one: no telemetry, no CDNs, no analytics, no
update pings. Remote images in email stay blocked until allowed. The website
mimux.dev sets zero cookies and uses self-hosted, cookieless analytics.
Full policy: <https://mimux.dev/privacy/>.

## Security

Report vulnerabilities privately via GitHub security advisories
(<https://github.com/mattmezza/mimux/security/advisories/new>) or
<mailto:security@mimux.dev>. Acknowledgement within 7 days. Only the latest
release receives fixes. Details: <https://mimux.dev/security/>.
